description:
Core technical skills that are highly useful
Data science / geospatial analysis — Working with NASA datasets (SMAP soil moisture, GPM/IMERG precipitation, Landsat & MODIS vegetation indices, ECOSTRESS, NASA POWER, GRACE, SRTM elevation, etc.). Experience with time-series analysis, vegetation indices (NDVI and related), soil-moisture/temperature trends, and climate indicators is especially valuable.
Python (or R) for data processing — Libraries such as xarray, rasterio, geopandas, rioxarray.
summary:
RotaClima is a deterministic agronomic decision-support web application built for the "Field Shift" challenge. Designed for farmers facing shifting climate regimes, it
    evaluates a farmer’s current crop rotation against up to three tailored alternatives—Adapted, Regenerative, and Diversified—without machine learning or black-box AI.
  
    Using 35 years (1991–2025) of daily NASA POWER agroclimatic data grouped by real agricultural seasons, RotaClima quantifies local climate shifts (Mann–Whitney U) and runs a 
    daily biophysical simulation combining FAO-56 Penman–Monteith ET0, USDA SCS-CN runoff, a 180-day soil-water spin-up, and EcoCrop/Teixeira thermal stress across 20 evaluation
    seasons. It outputs relative yield, plain-language failure risk ("bad season in X of 20"), and a 0–100 soil health score, alongside an offline NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 (250 m)    
    satellite backtest.
  
    RotaClima matters because farmers cannot risk livelihoods on unverified guesses or outdated planting calendars. Every metric is reproducible, linked directly to its         
    underlying NASA dataset and parameters, and transparent about statistical significance and modeling assumptions—empowering climate-resilient planting decisions in three     
    clicks.
details:
WHAT ROTACLIMA DOES & HOW IT WORKS

RotaClima is a deterministic agronomic decision-support system designed for the "Field Shift" challenge. A farmer selects a field location on an interactive map, chooses a

soil texture, and enters their current multi-year crop rotation.

RotaClima then fetches 35 years (1991-2025) of daily agroclimatic data from the NASA POWER API (10 parameters) and groups them by true agricultural seasons (starting July 1

in the Southern Hemisphere and January 1 in the Northern Hemisphere) rather than calendar years. The engine:

1. Detects Climate Shifts: Compares the first 15 seasons against the most recent 15 using a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (alpha = 0.10) across 14 agroclimatic metrics

(rainfall, rainy-season onset/cessation, extreme heat days above 35 C, dry spells, GDD, and ET0).

2. Simulates Crop & Soil Response: Runs a daily biophysical pipeline over 20 evaluation seasons (2005/06-2024/25) using FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET0 (with Hargreaves

fallback), a 180-day soil-water spin-up, USDA SCS-CN runoff, and EcoCrop / Teixeira et al. (2013) thermal-stress rules across a verified 13-crop catalog.

3. Compares Alternatives & Validates with Satellites: Evaluates the current rotation against up to three deterministic profiles—Adapted (minimum change), Regenerative (soil

restoration), and Diversified (2-year multi-family cycle)—and cross-checks stress seasons against an offline NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 (250 m NDVI) satellite backtest.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

- Actionable Risk Translation: Converts complex 35-year NASA climate series into clear metrics: relative yield, plain-language failure risk ("bad season in X of 20"), and a

0-100 soil health score.

- Full Traceability & Zero Hallucinations: Every number in a recommendation card is generated from deterministic templates and linked directly to its NASA dataset, parameter

name, unit, and period.

- Sustainable Dual Model: Individual farmers get 100% free, anonymous, paywall-free access (including offline/demo fallback for low-connectivity rural areas). Financial

sustainability comes from B2B integration with cooperatives, rural banks, and agricultural insurers (batch multi-field API, higher-resolution polygon rainfall, ENSO

weighting, and local yield/margin calibration).

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

- Backend & Scientific Engine: Python (>= 3.11), FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic v2, NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, HTTPX, and pytest (159 automated offline tests).

- Frontend & Visualization: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet (react-leaflet), and Recharts.

- NASA & Agronomic Standards: NASA POWER API, NASA ORNL MODIS MOD13Q1 v061, FAO-56, USDA SCS-CN (TR-55), and FAO EcoCrop.

CREATIVITY & KEY FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Physics Over Black-Box AI: We deliberately avoided generative AI or machine learning to prevent hallucinated numbers and overfitting on only 34 historical seasons. Farmers

cannot risk their livelihoods on opaque predictions.

- Scientific Honesty & Explicit Limits: Non-significant climate trends (p >= 0.10) are explicitly labeled "not significant," trade-offs are surfaced upfront (for example,

high-yield rotations that deplete soil nitrogen), and 12 explicit modeling assumptions (S1-S12)—such as the ~50 km regional scale of POWER and absence of invented market

prices—are transparently disclosed inside the product.
